subject: Investigation dossier & verified mitigation for CardinalPay incident
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: sara.lopez@cardinalpay.com, ops@cardinalpay.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Investigation dossier & verified mitigation for CardinalPay incident

Sara / CardinalPay ops team —

Thanks again for your patience while our teams completed the investigation into the May 17th tokenization latency spike that impacted a subset of your transactions. Attached is the investigation dossier we discussed: it contains a concise root-cause summary, a minute-by-minute timeline, log excerpts, the KV-cache eviction evidence set, and the verification steps we used to confirm the mitigation.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: an unexpected interaction between our prefix-KV eviction logic and a transient metadata write that temporarily increased cache churn for long-lived streams on the dedicated pool serving your region.
- Customer impact: elevated per-request latency and a small error rate increase for ~34 minutes across the east-us dedicated cluster; your traffic experienced ~0.6% additional timeouts during the window.
- Mitigation applied: conservative KV eviction threshold rollback + hotfix to avoid metadata-triggered eviction (deployed 17:46 PDT).
- Verification: rolling monitor checks and a follow-up synthetic run validated behavior returned to baseline within 12 minutes of the hotfix. Evidence links included below.

Action items for CardinalPay and Redwood (in the attached dossier and summarized below):
1) Redwood: deliver the KV eviction hardening patch to your Dedicated pool (done, build rwd-evic-1.4.2). Owner: Ben Carter. ETA: completed; patch deployed 2027-05-17 17:05 PDT.
2) Redwood: provide the full eviction logs + filtered request traces for your account (attachment: kvcache-eviction-logs-20270517.tar.gz). Owner: Monica Patel. ETA: attached.
3) CardinalPay: run your pre-production synthetic load against the dedicated endpoint with the updated patch and confirm no regression (we can help run this). Owner: CardinalPay ops. ETA: please confirm availability this week.
4) Joint: agree on an SLA credit calculation if the event meets the contractual window — I’ve opened a ticket with Finance (CP-2026-42).

I've included Ben and Monica on this message to verify the artifacts and to coordinate any follow-up. If you prefer a short run-through call to walk the dossier together, we can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Manager — Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0147
aisha.rahman@redwood.com

Attachments: cardinalpay-investigation-dossier.pdf (PDF, 1.9MB); kvcache-eviction-logs-20270517.tar.gz (logs, 120MB); timelines/cardinalpay_timeline_20270517-18.csv

Thanks Aisha — received and appreciate the level of detail in the dossier. Quick notes:
- We reviewed the timeline and the log excerpts. The impact described matches what our transaction team saw.
- We will run the pre-prod synthetic this afternoon and share results by end of day.
- Regarding the SLA credit: we need the full request-by-request UUID traces for 17:30–18:10 PDT to reconcile with our transaction logs. Can your team provide those filtered traces (PII stripped) and the verification checklist you ran?

Also — we'd like to schedule the 30 min call tomorrow at 10:00 PDT if that works for you and Ben.

Sara
Sara Lopez
Director of Platform Reliability — CardinalPay
ops@cardinalpay.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Sara —
Good call, I'll push the filtered request traces now and upload them to the shared drive with PII redaction. You'll see two artifacts: (1) request_traces_cardinalpay_1730-1810.csv (UUID, latency_ms, route, outcome) and (2) kvcache_eviction_context_1732-1756.log (eviction trigger lines and relevant metadata).

Verification checklist we ran (summary):
- Confirmed post-deploy baseline latency samples vs pre-incident baseline (30-min sliding window).
- Synthetic probe run simulating your 99th percentile payload sizes on a replicated Dedicated pool.
- KV eviction counts and TTL analysis validated lowered eviction churn after threshold rollback.
- Cross-checked with APM and request traces for error correlation.

I will upload artifacts to the Drive link and flag the items in the dossier. Call at 10:00 PDT tomorrow works for me.

Ben

ben.carter@redwood.com

Sara / team —
Artifacts uploaded here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3CardinalDossier (same link in the dossier metadata). Files uploaded: request_traces_cardinalpay_1730-1810.csv (PII redacted), kvcache_eviction_context_1732-1756.log, post-deploy-monitoring-snapshots.json.

Quick verification notes for your ops team to check on your side during the pre-prod run:
- Ensure synthetic uses sustained prefix lengths similar to production (we observed evictions when large prefix sets were actively written).
- Confirm 99th percentile latency <150ms for your test suite and no >0.3% timeout rate over 30 minutes.
- If you see any deviation, capture the request UUIDs and send them back — we’ll correlate with EVIC log markers and escalate to infra immediately.

Aisha will follow up on the SLA credit calculation ticket for your finance team. Looking forward to the call.

Regards,
Monica
